phase_0.boundary_condition: The reducing end anchor and the set of terminal leaves define the closed boundary of the glycan tree.

⊢.justification: The genesis of the glycan structure; the single point of attachment to the peptide bulk before any branching occurs.

⊣.justification: The closed boundary of the tree; the non-reducing ends where the chain terminates and no further branching is possible.

≻.justification: The directed morphism extending the chain from the reducing end toward the periphery; the forward growth of the glycan.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism; the descent or removal of terminal residues, reversing the growth direction.

⋈.justification: The sequential composition of sugar units; the chain of bonds connecting the reducing end to the leaves.

⊙.justification: The self-reference of each sugar unit; the specific stereochemical identity (e.g., GlcNAc vs Gal) that defines the node.

∈.justification: The co-multiplication where a single chain diverges into two or more distinct arms (e.g., a biantennary split).

∋.justification: The multiplication where multiple branches converge to form a single functional recognition surface or complex.

⊤.justification: The affirmative state where the glycan structure successfully engages a receptor with high fidelity.

⊥.justification: The negative state where the glycan structure fails to bind due to steric hindrance or incorrect orientation.

⊞.justification: The paradice state where the glycan simultaneously satisfies conflicting binding requirements or holds both bound and unbound states in a dynamic equilibrium.

⊡.justification: The irreversible fixation of the glycan structure; the high activation energy of glycosidic bonds prevents spontaneous rearrangement under physiological conditions.

phase_3.void_description: The state before the reducing end is attached to the peptide; no glycan exists.
phase_3.true_description: The glycan is fully assembled and successfully bound to its target receptor.
phase_3.false_description: The glycan is malformed, truncated, or sterically blocked from binding.
phase_3.both_description: The glycan exhibits dual specificity, binding to two different receptors simultaneously or existing in a dynamic equilibrium of bound/unbound states.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the system at the reducing end, the single point of attachment to the peptide backbone.
Establish the identity of the first monosaccharide unit (e.g., GlcNAc) at the reducing end.
Extend the chain forward via a glycosidic bond to the next monosaccharide.
Compose the linkage between the first and second sugar units.
Establish the identity of the second monosaccharide unit.
Encounter a branch point where the linear chain diverges into two distinct antennae.
Extend the first antenna arm forward from the branch point.
Compose the linkage within the first antenna arm.
Establish the identity of the sugar at the tip of the first antenna.
Reach the terminal leaf of the first antenna, closing this branch.
Extend the second antenna arm forward from the branch point.
Compose the linkage within the second antenna arm.
Establish the identity of the sugar at the tip of the second antenna.
Reach the terminal leaf of the second antenna, closing this branch.
Rejoin the two antenna arms at the receptor binding site to form a unified recognition surface.
Evaluate the affirmative state of high-affinity binding if the structure matches the receptor.
Evaluate the negative state of steric clash if the structure fails to fit.
Hold the paradice state if the glycan exhibits dual specificity or conflicting binding signals.
Fix the final state of the glycan complex, recording the irreversible kinetic freeze of the structure.
Close the entire system at the boundary of the glycan complex.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The enzymatic machinery (glycosyltransferases) that translates genetic instructions into specific glycan structures.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The glycosidic bonds that transmit structural information and steric constraints between monosaccharide units.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The stereochemical configuration (R/S) of each chiral center, stored in the rigid ring structure of the sugars.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The sequential order of glycosyltransferase action in the Golgi apparatus, determining the branching pattern.
phase_5.alfs_store: The set of eight mammalian N-glycan monosaccharides (GlcNAc, GalNAc, Mannose, Galactose, Glucose, Fucose, Sialic acid, Xylose) as the canonical reference.

phase_6.cycle_cost: The activation energy required to form glycosidic bonds, consumed during biosynthesis.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A disordered pool of activated sugar nucleotides and a peptide chain.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A highly ordered, kinetically frozen glycan tree attached to the peptide.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The system is entropy-conservative because the high activation energy of glycosidic bonds prevents spontaneous rearrangement, locking the structure in a low-entropy state that is maintained without continuous energy input.
